S50U26.today_summary: 1,070.7 closed -10.0 (-0.93%) and settled 0.7 points above the 1,070 max-pain strike, which has not moved in eight sessions. The drop pushed spot into the short-gamma pocket: cumulative net GEX at spot fell to -6,150 from Friday's -2,492, the deepest of the window, widening the amplifying zone below the 1,100 flip from 18.9 to 29.3 points. 14.44% ATM IV rose +1.47 to a window high and 25-delta skew re-steepened to +1.23, so the decline was paid for in volatility rather than faded. 74.3% of the +1,409 put OI build went to the 910/940 tail on 1,146 lots, while live near-money demand concentrated at 1,030 (+281 OI on 378 lots) and 1,050 (415 lots).
what_changed: Cumulative net GEX at spot -6,150 from -2,492, the deepest short-gamma pocket in eight sessions; the flip held 1,100, so the pocket widened from 18.9 to 29.3 points.
ATM IV +1.47 to 14.44%, the window high and the first print above 13.71%; the 1-sigma day expanded from 8.83 to 9.74 points.
25-delta skew +0.45 to +1.23 as the 1,040 put repriced to 15.37% against the 1,100 call at 14.14%; the 910 tail sits at 26.62%.
Put OI +1,409 to 38,946 (P/C OI 2.05 to 2.08, a window high) with +962 of it at the 910 strike on 972 lots, against +368 call OI.
S50U26.five_day_thesis: Five sessions took the anchor from 1,085.2 on 08-17 to 1,070.7, -14.5 points, while max pain never left 1,070 and the flip only stepped 1,100 to 1,110 and back to 1,100 - the structure absorbed the slide rather than repricing to it. The regime signal is the pocket, not the level: cumulative GEX at spot ran -1,999, -5,856, -5,905, -2,492, -6,150, so dealers have been amplifying all week and are deepest in it today, with no sign flip (total GEX stayed positive throughout, +2,931 to +6,337). Put OI grew 20.8% (32,232 to 38,946) against 6.7% on calls, and the 910 strike alone absorbed +3,573 of that - a persistent tail-hedging program, not a one-day reaction. IV broke the compression story that ran through 08-17: 12.50% to 14.44%, +1.94 points, with 25-delta skew widening from a flat +0.12 to +1.23. The one migration that matters is the call wall's 1,080 to 1,100 step on 08-20, which lifted the ceiling 20 points even as spot fell 14.5, leaving 1,050-1,100 as the week's working corridor.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1050 / 1020
strategies.rationale: Protection-zone insurance placed where the amplification actually lives: 1,050 is the live near put wall (1,745 OI on 415 lots) and the chain's most negative strike at -1,486 net GEX, so a break there has dealers hedging with the move rather than against it, and 1,020 is the 10-delta band. Note the cost has risen with the regime - 14.44% ATM IV is +1.47 above Friday, so this debit is dearer than the same structure a session ago.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit, roughly 6.8 points at 12.2 offered / 5.4 bid, capped by the 30-point width; breakeven 1,043.2, max gain 23.2 points.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close above 1,100 - the call wall and gamma flip stacked together - turns cumulative GEX positive and removes the downside amplification.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1020 / 990
strategies.rationale: Cheap convexity aimed where the flow is actually going: 74.3% of today's put OI build and 38.6% of put volume sat at or below 960, and the 910 strike has absorbed +3,573 contracts over five sessions at 26.62% IV. This spread sits inside the same short-gamma trough (1,030 to 1,050 carry -3,824 combined net GEX) at roughly half the debit of the near-money version.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit, roughly 3.2 points at 5.8 offered / 2.6 bid, capped by the 30-point width; breakeven 1,016.8, max gain 26.8 points.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close above 1,100, or the 910/940 tail OI ceasing to build - the Vol2Vol confirmation this structure leans on.

strategies.name: Call credit spread 1100 / 1120
strategies.rationale: 1,100 is simultaneously the call wall (2,805 OI on 646 lots, the chain's heaviest strike volume), the gamma flip, and the largest single-strike dampener at +3,038 net GEX - the best-defended level on the board, 29.3 points above spot. The honest caveat is that 14.14% call IV is the cheapest part of a put-rich surface, so this is a structural fade of a defended ceiling rather than a volatility sale, and the credit is thin against the risk.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point width less roughly 3.5 points of credit (7.4 bid / 3.9 offered) = 16.5 points, a 4.7-to-1 risk-to-credit ratio; breakeven 1,103.5.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close held above 1,100, which flips cumulative GEX positive and converts the wall from a dampener into a squeeze trigger.

S50U26.prediction: 1,050-1,100 is the working corridor: 1,070 max pain sits 0.7 points under spot and argues for chop, but with cumulative GEX at -6,150 the dealer book is amplifying rather than absorbing, so a break of 1,050 - the -1,486 net GEX strike and the live near put wall - should extend rather than mean-revert, with 9.74 points of 1-sigma daily range available. Upside is capped by the 1,100 wall-and-flip stack 29.3 points away, which has thickened by 334 contracts even as price fell. A daily close above 1,100 invalidates the downside tilt outright: cumulative GEX turns positive there and dealer hedging switches from amplifying to dampening.
S50U26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and no position size is implied. SET50 options are cash-settled on the SET50 index with no physical delivery, so the dealer-hedging mechanics behind pinning are structurally weaker than for share-settled single stocks: treat the 1,070 max-pain anchor as a tendency, not a magnet, and at 36 DTE pin logic barely applies at all. Defined risk is not risk-free - the stated max loss on each structure above is a real outcome - and a macro or news shock can override the option structure entirely.
